doors_basis: stores page lists 4 Paul Stuart stores, all US (NYC Madison Ave flagship, Chicago, Washington DC CityCenterDC, Southampton NY); no outlets, concessions or non-US stores listed. Japan (Tokyo Kita-Aoyama flagship and department-store shops) is run by licensee Sanyo Shokai per Wikipedia, not own doors, not counted.
owned_facility: claim only: Wool Plaid Robe PDP says robes are "handcrafted at our NYC Madison Avenue flagship store by our in-house tailors" (no photo, place detail or filing). Meet the Makers describes partner factories, not an owned one. Co-owner since Dec 2025 is Peerless Clothing (apparel manufacturer, per press); no product page says Peerless makes Paul Stuart goods.
named_makers: evidence on PDPs, small share: Rochester Tailored Clothing (Two Fifty Navy Blazer), Hamilton Shirts, Houston, "since 1883" (Made in America dress shirts, 5 styles), Mackintosh (Nor'easter cloth). Meet the Makers page names these plus Waterbury Button and American Woolen. 3 of 52 sampled PDPs name a maker; tailoring otherwise "Made in Canada"/"Made in Italy" with no maker.
named_mills: evidence on PDPs: Loro Piana (Double Faced Cashmere Coat; Cashmere Patch Pocket Jacket), Thomas Mason (Hamilton dress shirt), Somelos (Oxford Button-Down), American Woolen Mills CT (Two Fifty Blazer): 5 of 52 sampled PDPs. Others say only "Woven in Italy" / Biella. Made-to-measure page names Holland & Sherry, Loro Piana, Vitale Barberis Canonico, Solbiati (MTM cloth books, not product pages).
heritage_claim: claim, dated: homepage "American, Since 1938"; place implicit (Madison Avenue flagship, "New York Looks Good on You"); founder not named on site. Wikipedia (citing NYT 1981 obituary): founded 1938 by Ralph Ostrove, New York.
process_documented: partial: PDP construction bullets are specific (lightweight canvas, basted sleeve, felt under collar; Goodyear construction on shoes; split back yoke, single needle stitching, 2-ply yarn, handmade buttonholes on shirts). No page documents the brand's own making process; Meet the Makers is a visit narrative about partner factories.
craft_reasoning: Paul Stuart names makers and mills on product pages, but only for a minority of the range: Rochester Tailored Clothing, Hamilton Shirts with Thomas Mason cloth, Loro Piana, Somelos and Mackintosh appear on 5 of 52 sampled pages. 87% of sampled pages state a country, mainly Italy and Canada. The only owned-making statement is the in-house tailors claim on the robe page, with no evidence behind it, so this is a 3 (names makers and mills, owns nothing shown) rather than a 4.
founded_place: New York, NY (Madison Avenue at 45th Street)
founders: Ralph Ostrove (named the house for his son, Paul Stuart Ostrove; Wikipedia citing NYT)
owner_today: Middle West Partners (private investment group) with Peerless Clothing Inc., acquired from Mitsui & Co. (FashionNetwork, 24 Dec 2025); CEO John Hutchison (ex-Bonobos). Mitsui had owned it since Dec 2012 (Wikipedia citing New York Business Journal). Japan rights sold by Mitsui to Sanyo Shokai in 2021 (Wikipedia citing WWD).
